<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with clean framing. B (PRO) built the more attractive moral frame — who bears the cost of uncertainty, irreversibility of open weight release, and a strong tu quoque that CON's "regulators cannot verify" objection indicts the status quo GPAI chapter as well. But A (CON) won the decisive mechanism clash: licensing presupposes an artifact that can be characterised, a threshold that can be measured, and violations that can be detected, and A showed each of those is missing at the frontier. A's disanalogy to pharma (reproducible physical assays vs evaluations that flip with prompt phrasing) blunted B's best historical move (the efficacy-reform "requirements build the science" answer), and A converted B's own answer — thresholds codified from frameworks "the labs themselves already publish" — into a dilemma of rubber stamp or political instrument that B never resolved. A also handled B's toughest pressure question honestly ("None — the regimes don't compete at that layer") and turned it into the sharpest original claim of the debate: an unverifiable claim is safer as a disclosure with liability than as a certificate that teaches deployers to stop checking. B answered the open-weight dilemma inventively (license the release decision itself), but A's rejoinder that refusal merely relocates the release while shutting out only European open developers went largely unanswered, as did entrenchment and geofencing beyond one late line in the closing. B also incurred more execution cost, with two clipped over-length turns, one of which lost the single-market leverage argument entirely.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's answer to B's Q1: conceding that risk-based catches no frontier misrepresentation licensing would miss, then reframing — risk-based enforces where evidence and victims exist, while licensing makes the one undetectable capability claim the load-bearing wall and certifies uncertainty rather than disclosing it. Combined with A's pharma disanalogy on reproducible assays, this neutralised B's central tu quoque.</best_rebuttal>
